title: The phone book that led us to Assad's spy chief in hiding
excerpt: How we tracked down "The Spider" who was once one of the most-feared men in Syria.
content_html:
2 days ago

Alice CuddyBBC News

In an abandoned luxury apartment in the Syrian capital Damascus, armed men dressed in military fatigues sifted through designer clothes and documents.

Scattered across the living room floor, under a sparkling crystal chandelier, were dozens of photos of the same slender man in different settings - sitting at his desk, even playing in the snow. And multiple prints of the same image, showing him smiling warmly as he shook the hand of ousted dictator Bashar al-Assad.

The man was not instantly recognisable, but gold medals and gilded certificates piled nearby were inscribed with the name Hussam Luka.

Known as "The Spider", Luka was one of Assad's top henchmen, accused of orchestrating atrocities and systematic torture, and sanctioned by the UK, US and European Union.

As head of Syria's most powerful civilian intelligence agency, Luka was among the most feared men in the country. But much of his work was conducted from the shadows.

Like others in the regime, Luka seemingly vanished overnight in December 2024 when Assad was toppled, leaving a trail of unanswered questions and demands for justice that many fear will never be realised.

In his apartment, days after Assad's fall, we watched the rebels looking for clues as to where he might have gone.

In the corner of the living room, on a console table, was an unremarkable-looking notebook.

Inside, in scribbled blue handwriting, we found dozens of names - from shopkeepers and doctors, to military officials and people with the Luka family name.

Could these contacts help us learn more about The Spider and his crimes, or even help us to track him down?

At one time, Luka's own phone number was hard to avoid - in the early days of the Syrian civil war, it had been spray-painted on walls around the central city of Homs.

The conflict was sparked by Assad's brutal crushing of a pro-democracy uprising in 2011 - a war in which hundreds of thousands of people would go on to be killed.

Luka was a local head of the Political Security Directorate, one of Assad's main intelligence agencies, and had been given the task of wresting the city from the rebels.

At the time, rebel-held areas in Homs were under siege by the government, and residents were struggling to access food and medicine. Several people, including former rebel fighter Motaz al-Zaydi, told us they had resorted to eating rats.

Al-Zaydi remembers Luka's name and phone number appearing on a wall in his neighbourhood, and said the message began to spread that those wanting to flee the fighting could phone the number for safe passage.

Some are believed to have been granted safe transit out of the city by Luka, but others who called the number were never seen or heard from again, according to several people we spoke to, including al-Zaydi.

Many told us they referred to Luka as "The Spider" because of his vast web of allies and informants, including some embedded in rebel groups. "He was everywhere," Homs residents told us. Al-Zaydi described Luka as an "evil genius" and "a fox of a man".

But his most egregious action in the city, many argue, was his alleged involvement in the so-called Eid Massacre, known by some as the Children's Massacre, which the US noted when sanctioning him.

It was the Muslim holiday of Eid al-Adha in September 2015, and Mohammed Towakatli's seven-year-old, Wael, was gardening in the playground he had set up in the al-Waer neighbourhood.

At 17:10, just after the power ration had kicked in, Mohammed remembers the strike hitting.

As Mohammed walked around the park earlier this year, now planted with rows of saplings, he recalled the names of the children killed and the games they had been playing at the time, gesturing to the places where he had found their bodies, including that of Wael.

"They were tiny children," he said with tears in his eyes. "The ground here was painted red with blood."

Twenty-eight people were killed, including 17 children and four women, according to the Syrian Network for Human Rights.

Luka, according to a Syrian activist group, and a pro-opposition newspaper at the time, was responsible for the regime's selection of targets in the area that day.

His actions in Homs earned him a promotion, and by the time of the regime's collapse he ran the General Security Directorate (GSD) intelligence agency, making him one of the most powerful people in the country.

The government security services could target anyone - from opposition fighters, journalists, doctors, or rights activists, to people believed to be opposed in any form to the Assad government.

Those arrested were detained in Syria's political prisons, including Sednaya in Damascus - a facility so notorious it was dubbed the "human slaughterhouse". Many imprisoned there were never seen again.

As head of the GSD, Luka had strategic control over Syria's detention policies, and his personnel would monitor communications to and from Sednaya.

There are widespread calls across Syrian society on social media for former senior officials to be held accountable. Some also say the new Syrian government is not doing enough to bring these people to justice.

Syria's Attorney General, Hassan al-Turba, told the BBC the government had launched a lawsuit against Luka, accusing him of "premeditated murder, torture, and death resulting from torture".

"A warrant has been circulated domestically and we are working on circulating it internationally as well," he said, adding the administration was working to track the location and seek the extradition of Luka and other missing senior regime officials.

As he continues to grieve for his son, Mohammed told the BBC he wanted Luka, alongside other senior regime officials, to be returned to Syria and executed.

"They look like humans but have no humanity in them at all," he said.

We had taken photos of every page of the book we discovered in Luka's apartment and, back in London, began testing every one of its 155 numbers - aware that many people close to the regime would have fled or gone to ground. Fifty-one numbers appeared to be operational.

We then called these again in order of their apparent importance to Luka, starting with military commanders and relatives.

Every call was unsuccessful. Anyone who answered simply hung up when we explained who we were and what we wanted - or denied knowing Luka or his family, or even being the people listed in the book.

So a BBC reporter, whose own name was once on a GSD wanted list while Luka ran the agency, headed to Syria to try in person.

Many of those listed in the phone book were doctors, so our reporter began booking medical appointments with some of them as a way to meet them.

A doctor in Aleppo reluctantly acknowledged he had treated Luka, but then ordered our journalist to leave and returned his consultation fee.

Our reporter then booked an appointment with another doctor in the phone book, this time based in Damascus. This doctor revealed he had once accompanied Luka's mother on a medical trip to Russia, but was reluctant to give us any more information, other than to vaguely direct us to a pharmacy belonging to one of Luka's daughters.

Locals said she, too, had not been seen since December 2024.

For months we drew a blank in our hunt for Luka.

And then we had our first breakthrough.

One of those listed in the book, who we tried calling again, finally answered the phone.

He had been the guard for Luka's apartment block, he told us, and eventually agreed to give us the number for someone he said had been Luka's personal bodyguard - a man we are calling Mahmoud.

It took weeks to secure an interview with Mahmoud. Meetings would be scheduled but he would not show up, or he would request a meeting in a private space such as a car or apartment, which our reporter judged too much of a risk.

They eventually met at a hotel one night, just before midnight. Broad-shouldered and physically imposing, Mahmoud seemed to be considering every answer carefully before he spoke.

He told us he was angry with Luka for leaving him behind when the regime fell. As word had spread in December 2024 that Assad's rule was on the brink of collapse - with rebels advancing on the capital - Luka had said he would stay and defend Damascus, Mahmoud told us. But by the early hours of the next morning, Luka had disappeared, taking a large sum of money with him from the office safe, Mahmoud said.

Mahmoud refused to share any contact details for Luka or his family, but did give us a number for Luka's driver, who he believed had driven the former spy chief out of the capital that night.

This man proved even harder to reach.

When he answered the phone, his voice was nervous and unsteady. He repeatedly insisted he was just a driver, and knew nothing of Luka's activities. Multiple meetings with us were never kept, and eventually he stopped replying.

We turned our attention to Luka's possible escape routes, including neighbouring Lebanon - where the Iran-backed group Hezbollah had close links with the Assad regime.

One senior source in the Lebanese government told us he understood Luka had passed through Lebanon on a "good Russian passport but with a different name", before flying out to Russia.

We managed to find a man, now based in Lebanon, whose name was listed in Luka's contacts book, but under a number that no longer worked. He is one of many wanted by the new Syrian government, because of his close association with the Assad regime.

This man, who we cannot identify, said he had a number for Luka.

We saw it, and realised it had a Russian country code.

Russia was a key backer of the Assad regime, and in the days after his fall, Assad released a statement confirming that he had fled there. Many of his inner circle were believed to have followed him.

Back in Luka's apartment in Damascus, we had found clues that Luka also had strong links to Moscow - awards from Russia's foreign spy service, and even a New Year's card addressed to him from a senior Russian official.

Now, the Russian telephone number for him suggested we finally had proof that he was - as we had predicted - in Russia.

We wanted to verify that this number really was Luka's.

So a few days later, with us present, the man agreed to put the person he said was Hussam Luka on speakerphone, and ask him questions which we believed only Luka would know the answer to, based on information we had gathered during our investigation.

The voice on the other end of the phone sounded confused, but answered the questions instantly and correctly.

He refused, however, to speak to us directly.

But our contact later agreed to call Luka again and allow us to try to interview him.

The same voice answered, and we introduced ourselves, explaining that we had questions about serious allegations relating to massacres and torture committed by the former regime official.

"I can't take any risk talking on the phone in the position I'm in," Luka said, his tone anxious.

Asked if Russia was blocking him from talking, Luka said: "I cannot talk. I can't explain. You have to understand."

When asked if he would meet us outside Russia, he said: "It's difficult."

He then hung up the phone.

We later obtained a second number which we were told was also for Luka - this time registered in Syria and linked to social media and messaging apps which he appeared to be still using.

Over a period of a day, the BBC was able to locate him in two ​suburban areas on the outskirts of the Russian capital, Moscow.

The locations seemed far removed from the luxurious lifestyle Assad is reported to be leading in exile in Russia, and to the life Luka himself once led in Syria.

We knew we could not approach him in person in Russia, where Assad's henchmen are shielded from international journalists and police, so we decided to try putting our allegations to him over the phone once again.

We rang the number and the same voice as before answered, the line crackly.

He asked who was calling, and when told it was the BBC, he immediately hung up.

We sent a message over WhatsApp, asking for his response to the many allegations against him, but he did not reply.

Confirmation that Luka is in Moscow is difficult news for those in Syria seeking justice. Russia is highly unlikely to extradite officials from the regime that it long supported.

The Russian government did not respond to BBC requests for comment about Luka's presence there, or whether it would ever consider an extradition request.

Back in Homs, Mohammed says he will never let go of the hope that Luka, and other senior members of the Assad regime, will one day face justice.

"[I am] angry at all those who were with the regime and its security apparatus… They were all against us," he says.

"Wael was just a seven-year-old child… All he cared about was playing and having fun."

Additional reporting by Riam Dalati, Ghaith Solh and Abigail Akerman

sentences.zh: 这场冲突是由2011年阿萨德残酷镇压一场支持民主的起义引发的——这场战争导致数十万人丧生。

blocks.html_en: Luka was a local head of the Political Security Directorate, one of Assad's main intelligence agencies, and had been given the task of wresting the city from the rebels.

sentences.en: Luka was a local head of the Political Security Directorate, one of Assad's main intelligence agencies, and had been given the task of wresting the city from the rebels.
sentences.zh: 卢卡是阿萨德主要情报机构之一政治安全局的当地负责人，并被赋予从叛乱分子手中夺取这座城市的任务。

blocks.html_en: At the time, rebel-held areas in Homs were under siege by the government, and residents were struggling to access food and medicine. Several people, including former rebel fighter Motaz al-Zaydi, told us they had resorted to eating rats.

sentences.en: At the time, rebel-held areas in Homs were under siege by the government, and residents were struggling to access food and medicine.
sentences.zh: 当时，霍姆斯叛军控制的地区遭到政府围困，居民难以获取食物和药品。

sentences.en: Several people, including former rebel fighter Motaz al-Zaydi, told us they had resorted to eating rats.
sentences.zh: 包括前叛军战士莫塔兹·扎伊迪在内的几个人告诉我们，他们已经开始吃老鼠了。

blocks.html_en: Al-Zaydi remembers Luka's name and phone number appearing on a wall in his neighbourhood, and said the message began to spread that those wanting to flee the fighting could phone the number for safe passage.

sentences.en: Al-Zaydi remembers Luka's name and phone number appearing on a wall in his neighbourhood, and said the message began to spread that those wanting to flee the fighting could phone the number for safe passage.
sentences.zh: 扎伊迪记得卢卡的名字和电话号码出现在他家附近的墙上，并表示消息开始传播，那些想要逃离战斗的人可以拨打该号码以确保安全。

blocks.html_en: Some are believed to have been granted safe transit out of the city by Luka, but others who called the number were never seen or heard from again, according to several people we spoke to, including al-Zaydi.

sentences.en: Some are believed to have been granted safe transit out of the city by Luka, but others who called the number were never seen or heard from again, according to several people we spoke to, including al-Zaydi.
sentences.zh: 据我们采访的几位人士（包括扎伊迪）称，据信卢卡已批准一些人安全出城，但拨打该号码的其他人却再也没有出现或音讯。

blocks.html_en: Many told us they referred to Luka as "The Spider" because of his vast web of allies and informants, including some embedded in rebel groups. "He was everywhere," Homs residents told us. Al-Zaydi described Luka as an "evil genius" and "a fox of a man".

sentences.en: Many told us they referred to Luka as "The Spider" because of his vast web of allies and informants, including some embedded in rebel groups.
sentences.zh: 许多人告诉我们，他们将卢卡称为“蜘蛛”，因为他拥有庞大的盟友和线人网络，其中包括一些嵌入反叛组织的人。

sentences.en: "He was everywhere," Homs residents told us.
sentences.zh: “他无处不在，”霍姆斯居民告诉我们。

sentences.en: Al-Zaydi described Luka as an "evil genius" and "a fox of a man".
sentences.zh: 扎伊迪将卢卡形容为“邪恶的天才”和“人中的狐狸”。

blocks.html_en: But his most egregious action in the city, many argue, was his alleged involvement in the so-called Eid Massacre, known by some as the Children's Massacre, which the US noted when sanctioning him.

sentences.en: But his most egregious action in the city, many argue, was his alleged involvement in the so-called Eid Massacre, known by some as the Children's Massacre, which the US noted when sanctioning him.
sentences.zh: 但许多人认为，他在这座城市最令人震惊的行为是他涉嫌参与所谓的开斋节大屠杀，一些人将其称为“儿童大屠杀”，美国在制裁他时指出了这一点。

blocks.html_en: It was the Muslim holiday of Eid al-Adha in September 2015, and Mohammed Towakatli's seven-year-old, Wael, was gardening in the playground he had set up in the al-Waer neighbourhood.

sentences.en: It was the Muslim holiday of Eid al-Adha in September 2015, and Mohammed Towakatli's seven-year-old, Wael, was gardening in the playground he had set up in the al-Waer neighbourhood.
sentences.zh: 2015 年 9 月，正值穆斯林节日古尔邦节，穆罕默德·托瓦卡特利 (Mohammed Towakatli) 7 岁的孩子瓦尔 (Wael) 正在他在瓦尔 (al-Waer) 社区搭建的操场上园艺。

blocks.html_en: At 17:10, just after the power ration had kicked in, Mohammed remembers the strike hitting.

sentences.en: At 17:10, just after the power ration had kicked in, Mohammed remembers the strike hitting.
sentences.zh: 17点10分，就在电力配给开始后，穆罕默德记得罢工发生了。

blocks.html_en: As Mohammed walked around the park earlier this year, now planted with rows of saplings, he recalled the names of the children killed and the games they had been playing at the time, gesturing to the places where he had found their bodies, including that of Wael.

sentences.en: As Mohammed walked around the park earlier this year, now planted with rows of saplings, he recalled the names of the children killed and the games they had been playing at the time, gesturing to the places where he had found their bodies, including that of Wael.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，穆罕默德在公园里散步时，公园里种满了树苗，他回忆起被杀儿童的名字和他们当时玩的游戏，并指着他发现他们尸体的地方，包括瓦尔的地方。

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>Mohammed at the grave of his son, who was killed in a bombing in Homs </figcaption>

sentences.en: Mohammed at the grave of his son, who was killed in a bombing in Homs
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德在他儿子的坟墓前，他的儿子在霍姆斯的爆炸中丧生

blocks.html_en: "They were tiny children," he said with tears in his eyes. "The ground here was painted red with blood."

sentences.en: "They were tiny children," he said with tears in his eyes.
sentences.zh: “他们都是小孩子，”他眼里含着泪水说道。

sentences.en: "The ground here was painted red with blood."
sentences.zh: “这里的地面被鲜血染红了。”

blocks.html_en: Twenty-eight people were killed, including 17 children and four women, according to the Syrian Network for Human Rights.

sentences.en: Twenty-eight people were killed, including 17 children and four women, according to the Syrian Network for Human Rights.
sentences.zh: 据叙利亚人权网络称，共有 28 人死亡，其中包括 17 名儿童和 4 名妇女。

blocks.html_en: Luka, according to a Syrian activist group, and a pro-opposition newspaper at the time, was responsible for the regime's selection of targets in the area that day.

sentences.en: Luka, according to a Syrian activist group, and a pro-opposition newspaper at the time, was responsible for the regime's selection of targets in the area that day.
sentences.zh: 据叙利亚活动组织和当时的亲反对派报纸称，卢卡负责叙利亚政权当天在该地区选择的目标。

blocks.html_en: His actions in Homs earned him a promotion, and by the time of the regime's collapse he ran the General Security Directorate (GSD) intelligence agency, making him one of the most powerful people in the country.

sentences.en: His actions in Homs earned him a promotion, and by the time of the regime's collapse he ran the General Security Directorate (GSD) intelligence agency, making him one of the most powerful people in the country.
sentences.zh: 他在霍姆斯的行动为他赢得了晋升，到政权垮台时，他负责管理安全总局（GSD）情报机构，使他成为该国最有权势的人之一。

blocks.html_en: The government security services could target anyone - from opposition fighters, journalists, doctors, or rights activists, to people believed to be opposed in any form to the Assad government.

sentences.en: The government security services could target anyone - from opposition fighters, journalists, doctors, or rights activists, to people believed to be opposed in any form to the Assad government.
sentences.zh: 政府安全部门可以针对任何人——从反对派战士、记者、医生或维权人士，到据信以任何形式反对阿萨德政府的人。

blocks.html_en: Those arrested were detained in Syria's political prisons, including Sednaya in Damascus - a facility so notorious it was dubbed the "human slaughterhouse". Many imprisoned there were never seen again.

sentences.en: Those arrested were detained in Syria's political prisons, including Sednaya in Damascus - a facility so notorious it was dubbed the "human slaughterhouse".
sentences.zh: 被捕者被关押在叙利亚政治监狱，其中包括大马士革的塞德纳亚监狱，该监狱臭名昭著，被称为“人类屠宰场”。

sentences.en: Many imprisoned there were never seen again.
sentences.zh: 许多被囚禁在那里的人再也没有见过。

blocks.html_en: As head of the GSD, Luka had strategic control over Syria's detention policies, and his personnel would monitor communications to and from Sednaya.

sentences.en: As head of the GSD, Luka had strategic control over Syria's detention policies, and his personnel would monitor communications to and from Sednaya.
sentences.zh: 作为总安全局局长，卢卡对叙利亚的拘留政策拥有战略控制权，他的人员将监控塞德纳亚的来往通讯。

blocks.html_en: There are widespread calls across Syrian society on social media for former senior officials to be held accountable. Some also say the new Syrian government is not doing enough to bring these people to justice.

sentences.en: There are widespread calls across Syrian society on social media for former senior officials to be held accountable.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体上叙利亚社会广泛呼吁追究前高级官员的责任。

sentences.en: Some also say the new Syrian government is not doing enough to bring these people to justice.
sentences.zh: 一些人还表示，叙利亚新政府在将这些人绳之以法方面做得不够。

blocks.html_en: Syria's Attorney General, Hassan al-Turba, told the BBC the government had launched a lawsuit against Luka, accusing him of "premeditated murder, torture, and death resulting from torture".

sentences.en: Syria's Attorney General, Hassan al-Turba, told the BBC the government had launched a lawsuit against Luka, accusing him of "premeditated murder, torture, and death resulting from torture".
sentences.zh: 叙利亚总检察长哈桑·图尔巴告诉英国广播公司，政府已对卢卡提起诉讼，指控他“有预谋的谋杀、酷刑和酷刑造成的死亡”。

blocks.html_en: "A warrant has been circulated domestically and we are working on circulating it internationally as well," he said, adding the administration was working to track the location and seek the extradition of Luka and other missing senior regime officials.

sentences.en: "A warrant has been circulated domestically and we are working on circulating it internationally as well," he said, adding the administration was working to track the location and seek the extradition of Luka and other missing senior regime officials.
sentences.zh: 他说：“逮捕令已在国内发出，我们正在努力在国际上发出逮捕令。”他补充说，政府正在努力追踪该地点并寻求引渡卢卡和其他失踪的政权高级官员。

blocks.html_en: As he continues to grieve for his son, Mohammed told the BBC he wanted Luka, alongside other senior regime officials, to be returned to Syria and executed.

sentences.en: As he continues to grieve for his son, Mohammed told the BBC he wanted Luka, alongside other senior regime officials, to be returned to Syria and executed.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德继续为儿子哀悼，他告诉英国广播公司，他希望卢卡和其他政权高级官员一起被送回叙利亚并被处决。

blocks.html_en: "They look like humans but have no humanity in them at all," he said.

sentences.en: "They look like humans but have no humanity in them at all," he said.
sentences.zh: “他们看起来像人类，但根本没有人性，”他说。

blocks.html_en: We had taken photos of every page of the book we discovered in Luka's apartment and, back in London, began testing every one of its 155 numbers - aware that many people close to the regime would have fled or gone to ground. Fifty-one numbers appeared to be operational.

sentences.en: We had taken photos of every page of the book we discovered in Luka's apartment and, back in London, began testing every one of its 155 numbers - aware that many people close to the regime would have fled or gone to ground.
sentences.zh: 我们对在卢卡公寓发现的书的每一页都拍了照片，然后回到伦敦，开始测试其中 155 个号码中的每一个号码 - 意识到许多与政权关系密切的人可能已经逃走或转入地面。

sentences.en: Fifty-one numbers appeared to be operational.
sentences.zh: 五十一个号码似乎可以使用。

blocks.html_en: We then called these again in order of their apparent importance to Luka, starting with military commanders and relatives.

sentences.en: We then called these again in order of their apparent importance to Luka, starting with military commanders and relatives.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们按照对卢卡的明显重要性顺序再次称呼这些人，从军事指挥官和亲属开始。

blocks.html_en: Every call was unsuccessful. Anyone who answered simply hung up when we explained who we were and what we wanted - or denied knowing Luka or his family, or even being the people listed in the book.

sentences.en: Every call was unsuccessful.
sentences.zh: 每次呼叫都没有成功。

sentences.en: Anyone who answered simply hung up when we explained who we were and what we wanted - or denied knowing Luka or his family, or even being the people listed in the book.
sentences.zh: 当我们解释我们是谁以及我们想要什么时，任何接听电话的人都会挂断电话，或者否认认识卢卡或他的家人，甚至否认自己是书中列出的人。

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>The phone book we found in the apartment - the BBC has redacted the surnames and the first three digits of each phone number   </figcaption>

sentences.en: The phone book we found in the apartment - the BBC has redacted the surnames and the first three digits of each phone number
sentences.zh: 我们在公寓里找到的电话簿 - BBC 已编辑了姓氏和每个电话号码的前三位数字

blocks.html_en: So a BBC reporter, whose own name was once on a GSD wanted list while Luka ran the agency, headed to Syria to try in person.

sentences.en: So a BBC reporter, whose own name was once on a GSD wanted list while Luka ran the agency, headed to Syria to try in person.
sentences.zh: 因此，一名 BBC 记者（在卢卡负责管理该机构期间，他的名字曾经出现在 GSD 的通缉名单上）亲自前往叙利亚进行尝试。

blocks.html_en: Many of those listed in the phone book were doctors, so our reporter began booking medical appointments with some of them as a way to meet them.

sentences.en: Many of those listed in the phone book were doctors, so our reporter began booking medical appointments with some of them as a way to meet them.
sentences.zh: 电话簿中列出的许多人都是医生，因此我们的记者开始为其中一些人预约医疗预约，以与他们会面。

blocks.html_en: A doctor in Aleppo reluctantly acknowledged he had treated Luka, but then ordered our journalist to leave and returned his consultation fee.

sentences.en: A doctor in Aleppo reluctantly acknowledged he had treated Luka, but then ordered our journalist to leave and returned his consultation fee.
sentences.zh: 阿勒颇的一名医生不情愿地承认自己曾治疗过卢卡，但随后命令记者离开，并退还了咨询费。

blocks.html_en: Our reporter then booked an appointment with another doctor in the phone book, this time based in Damascus. This doctor revealed he had once accompanied Luka's mother on a medical trip to Russia, but was reluctant to give us any more information, other than to vaguely direct us to a pharmacy belonging to one of Luka's daughters.

sentences.en: Our reporter then booked an appointment with another doctor in the phone book, this time based in Damascus.
sentences.zh: 我们的记者随后在电话簿中预约了另一位医生，这次是在大马士革。

sentences.en: This doctor revealed he had once accompanied Luka's mother on a medical trip to Russia, but was reluctant to give us any more information, other than to vaguely direct us to a pharmacy belonging to one of Luka's daughters.
sentences.zh: 这位医生透露，他曾陪同卢卡的母亲前往俄罗斯就医，但不愿向我们提供更多信息，只是含糊地引导我们前往卢卡女儿之一的药房。

blocks.html_en: Locals said she, too, had not been seen since December 2024.

sentences.en: Locals said she, too, had not been seen since December 2024.
sentences.zh: 当地人称，自 2024 年 12 月以来，她也没有再出现过。

blocks.html_en: For months we drew a blank in our hunt for Luka.

sentences.en: For months we drew a blank in our hunt for Luka.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，我们在寻找卢卡的过程中一直一片空白。

blocks.html_en: And then we had our first breakthrough.

sentences.en: And then we had our first breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 然后我们取得了第一个突破。

blocks.html_en: One of those listed in the book, who we tried calling again, finally answered the phone.

sentences.en: One of those listed in the book, who we tried calling again, finally answered the phone.
sentences.zh: 我们再次尝试给书中列出的一位人士打电话，他终于接了电话。

blocks.html_en: He had been the guard for Luka's apartment block, he told us, and eventually agreed to give us the number for someone he said had been Luka's personal bodyguard - a man we are calling Mahmoud.

sentences.en: He had been the guard for Luka's apartment block, he told us, and eventually agreed to give us the number for someone he said had been Luka's personal bodyguard - a man we are calling Mahmoud.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我们，他曾是卢卡公寓楼的警卫，并最终同意向我们提供他所说的卢卡私人保镖的电话号码——我们称之为马哈茂德。

blocks.html_en: It took weeks to secure an interview with Mahmoud. Meetings would be scheduled but he would not show up, or he would request a meeting in a private space such as a car or apartment, which our reporter judged too much of a risk.

sentences.en: It took weeks to secure an interview with Mahmoud.
sentences.zh: 花了几周时间才获得对马哈茂德的采访。

sentences.en: Meetings would be scheduled but he would not show up, or he would request a meeting in a private space such as a car or apartment, which our reporter judged too much of a risk.
sentences.zh: 会议会安排好，但他不会出现，或者他会要求在汽车或公寓等私人空间举行会议，我们的记者认为这样做风险太大。

blocks.html_en: They eventually met at a hotel one night, just before midnight. Broad-shouldered and physically imposing, Mahmoud seemed to be considering every answer carefully before he spoke.

sentences.en: They eventually met at a hotel one night, just before midnight.
sentences.zh: 他们最终在一天晚上午夜之前在一家酒店见面。

sentences.en: Broad-shouldered and physically imposing, Mahmoud seemed to be considering every answer carefully before he spoke.
sentences.zh: 马哈茂德肩膀宽阔，体格魁梧，说话前似乎仔细考虑了每一个答案。

blocks.html_en: He told us he was angry with Luka for leaving him behind when the regime fell. As word had spread in December 2024 that Assad's rule was on the brink of collapse - with rebels advancing on the capital - Luka had said he would stay and defend Damascus, Mahmoud told us. But by the early hours of the next morning, Luka had disappeared, taking a large sum of money with him from the office safe, Mahmoud said.

sentences.en: He told us he was angry with Luka for leaving him behind when the regime fell.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我们，他对卢卡在政权倒台后抛弃他感到愤怒。

sentences.en: As word had spread in December 2024 that Assad's rule was on the brink of collapse - with rebels advancing on the capital - Luka had said he would stay and defend Damascus, Mahmoud told us.
sentences.zh: 马哈茂德告诉我们，随着 2024 年 12 月有消息传出，阿萨德的统治正处于崩溃的边缘，叛军正在向首都挺进，卢卡曾表示他将留下来保卫大马士革。

sentences.en: But by the early hours of the next morning, Luka had disappeared, taking a large sum of money with him from the office safe, Mahmoud said.
sentences.zh: 但马哈茂德说，到第二天凌晨，卢卡就失踪了，并从办公室保险箱中带走了一大笔钱。

blocks.html_en: Mahmoud refused to share any contact details for Luka or his family, but did give us a number for Luka's driver, who he believed had driven the former spy chief out of the capital that night.

sentences.en: Mahmoud refused to share any contact details for Luka or his family, but did give us a number for Luka's driver, who he believed had driven the former spy chief out of the capital that night.
sentences.zh: 马哈茂德拒绝透露卢卡或他家人的任何联系方式，但给了我们卢卡司机的电话号码，他相信当晚司机将这位前间谍头子赶出了首都。

blocks.html_en: This man proved even harder to reach.

sentences.en: This man proved even harder to reach.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这个人更难接近。

blocks.html_en: When he answered the phone, his voice was nervous and unsteady. He repeatedly insisted he was just a driver, and knew nothing of Luka's activities. Multiple meetings with us were never kept, and eventually he stopped replying.

sentences.en: When he answered the phone, his voice was nervous and unsteady.
sentences.zh: 当他接电话时，他的声音紧张而不稳定。

sentences.en: He repeatedly insisted he was just a driver, and knew nothing of Luka's activities.
sentences.zh: 他一再坚称自己只是一名司机，对卢卡的活动一无所知。

sentences.en: Multiple meetings with us were never kept, and eventually he stopped replying.
sentences.zh: 与我们的多次会面从未保留，最终他不再回复。

blocks.html_en: We turned our attention to Luka's possible escape routes, including neighbouring Lebanon - where the Iran-backed group Hezbollah had close links with the Assad regime.

sentences.en: We turned our attention to Luka's possible escape routes, including neighbouring Lebanon - where the Iran-backed group Hezbollah had close links with the Assad regime.
sentences.zh: 我们将注意力转向卢卡可能的逃亡路线，包括邻国黎巴嫩——伊朗支持的真主党在黎巴嫩与阿萨德政权有着密切的联系。

blocks.html_en: One senior source in the Lebanese government told us he understood Luka had passed through Lebanon on a "good Russian passport but with a different name", before flying out to Russia.

sentences.en: One senior source in the Lebanese government told us he understood Luka had passed through Lebanon on a "good Russian passport but with a different name", before flying out to Russia.
sentences.zh: 黎巴嫩政府的一位高级消息人士告诉我们，他了解到卢卡在飞往俄罗斯之前持“良好的俄罗斯护照，但名字不同”经过黎巴嫩。

blocks.html_en: We managed to find a man, now based in Lebanon, whose name was listed in Luka's contacts book, but under a number that no longer worked. He is one of many wanted by the new Syrian government, because of his close association with the Assad regime.

sentences.en: We managed to find a man, now based in Lebanon, whose name was listed in Luka's contacts book, but under a number that no longer worked.
sentences.zh: 我们设法找到了一名现居黎巴嫩的男子，他的名字列在卢卡的通讯录中，但号码已失效。

sentences.en: He is one of many wanted by the new Syrian government, because of his close association with the Assad regime.
sentences.zh: 由于他与阿萨德政权关系密切，他是叙利亚新政府通缉的众多人之一。

blocks.html_en: This man, who we cannot identify, said he had a number for Luka.

sentences.en: This man, who we cannot identify, said he had a number for Luka.
sentences.zh: 我们无法确认这名男子的身份，他说他有卢卡的电话号码。

blocks.html_en: We saw it, and realised it had a Russian country code.

sentences.en: We saw it, and realised it had a Russian country code.

content_html_zh:
2天前

爱丽丝·卡迪BBC 新闻

在叙利亚首都大马士革的一间废弃的豪华公寓里，穿着军装的武装人员正在仔细检查名牌服装和文件。

客厅的地板上，一盏闪闪发光的水晶吊灯下，散落着几十张同一个身材苗条的男人在不同场景下的照片——坐在办公桌前，甚至在雪地里玩耍。 还有同一张照片的多张照片，显示他在与被驱逐的独裁者巴沙尔·阿萨德握手时热情地微笑着。

这名男子并没有被立即认出，但附近堆放的金牌和镀金证书上刻着胡萨姆·卢卡（Hussam Luka）的名字。

卢卡被称为“蜘蛛”，是阿萨德的高级追随者之一，被指控策划暴行和系统性酷刑，并受到英国、美国和欧盟的制裁。

作为叙利亚最强大的民事情报机构的负责人，卢卡是该国最令人畏惧的人之一。 但他的大部分工作都是在暗处进行的。

与该政权中的其他人一样，卢卡似乎在 2024 年 12 月阿萨德被推翻时一夜之间消失了，留下了一系列悬而未决的问题和正义要求，许多人担心这些问题和正义永远不会实现。

阿萨德倒台几天后，在他的公寓里，我们看到叛军寻找他可能去了哪里的线索。

客厅一角的玄关桌上，放着一本看上去不起眼的笔记本。

在里面，我们发现了几十个潦草的蓝色字迹的名字——从店主和医生，到军官和卢卡姓氏的人。

这些联系可以帮助我们更多地了解蜘蛛和他的罪行，甚至帮助我们追踪他吗？

曾经，卢卡自己的电话号码很难避免——在叙利亚内战初期，它被喷漆在中心城市霍姆斯周围的墙上。

这场冲突是由2011年阿萨德残酷镇压一场支持民主的起义引发的——这场战争导致数十万人丧生。

卢卡是阿萨德主要情报机构之一政治安全局的当地负责人，并被赋予从叛乱分子手中夺取这座城市的任务。

当时，霍姆斯叛军控制的地区遭到政府围困，居民难以获取食物和药品。 包括前叛军战士莫塔兹·扎伊迪在内的几个人告诉我们，他们已经开始吃老鼠了。

扎伊迪记得卢卡的名字和电话号码出现在他家附近的墙上，并表示消息开始传播，那些想要逃离战斗的人可以拨打该号码以确保安全。

据我们采访的几位人士（包括扎伊迪）称，据信卢卡已批准一些人安全出城，但拨打该号码的其他人却再也没有出现或音讯。

许多人告诉我们，他们将卢卡称为“蜘蛛”，因为他拥有庞大的盟友和线人网络，其中包括一些嵌入反叛组织的人。 “他无处不在，”霍姆斯居民告诉我们。 扎伊迪将卢卡形容为“邪恶的天才”和“人中的狐狸”。

但许多人认为，他在这座城市最令人震惊的行为是他涉嫌参与所谓的开斋节大屠杀，一些人将其称为“儿童大屠杀”，美国在制裁他时指出了这一点。

2015 年 9 月，正值穆斯林节日古尔邦节，穆罕默德·托瓦卡特利 (Mohammed Towakatli) 7 岁的孩子瓦尔 (Wael) 正在他在瓦尔 (al-Waer) 社区搭建的操场上园艺。

17点10分，就在电力配给开始后，穆罕默德记得罢工发生了。

今年早些时候，穆罕默德在公园里散步时，公园里种满了树苗，他回忆起被杀儿童的名字和他们当时玩的游戏，并指着他发现他们尸体的地方，包括瓦尔的地方。

“他们都是小孩子，”他眼里含着泪水说道。 “这里的地面被鲜血染红了。”

据叙利亚人权网络称，共有 28 人死亡，其中包括 17 名儿童和 4 名妇女。

据叙利亚活动组织和当时的亲反对派报纸称，卢卡负责叙利亚政权当天在该地区选择的目标。

他在霍姆斯的行动为他赢得了晋升，到政权垮台时，他负责管理安全总局（GSD）情报机构，使他成为该国最有权势的人之一。

政府安全部门可以针对任何人——从反对派战士、记者、医生或维权人士，到据信以任何形式反对阿萨德政府的人。

被捕者被关押在叙利亚政治监狱，其中包括大马士革的塞德纳亚监狱，该监狱臭名昭著，被称为“人类屠宰场”。 许多被囚禁在那里的人再也没有见过。

作为总安全局局长，卢卡对叙利亚的拘留政策拥有战略控制权，他的人员将监控塞德纳亚的来往通讯。

社交媒体上叙利亚社会广泛呼吁追究前高级官员的责任。 一些人还表示，叙利亚新政府在将这些人绳之以法方面做得不够。

叙利亚总检察长哈桑·图尔巴告诉英国广播公司，政府已对卢卡提起诉讼，指控他“有预谋的谋杀、酷刑和酷刑造成的死亡”。

他说：“逮捕令已在国内发出，我们正在努力在国际上发出逮捕令。”他补充说，政府正在努力追踪该地点并寻求引渡卢卡和其他失踪的政权高级官员。

穆罕默德继续为儿子哀悼，他告诉英国广播公司，他希望卢卡和其他政权高级官员一起被送回叙利亚并被处决。

“他们看起来像人类，但根本没有人性，”他说。

我们对在卢卡公寓发现的书的每一页都拍了照片，然后回到伦敦，开始测试其中 155 个号码中的每一个号码 - 意识到许多与政权关系密切的人可能已经逃走或转入地面。 五十一个号码似乎可以使用。

然后，我们按照对卢卡的明显重要性顺序再次称呼这些人，从军事指挥官和亲属开始。

每次呼叫都没有成功。 当我们解释我们是谁以及我们想要什么时，任何接听电话的人都会挂断电话，或者否认认识卢卡或他的家人，甚至否认自己是书中列出的人。

因此，一名 BBC 记者（在卢卡负责管理该机构期间，他的名字曾经出现在 GSD 的通缉名单上）亲自前往叙利亚进行尝试。

电话簿中列出的许多人都是医生，因此我们的记者开始为其中一些人预约医疗预约，以与他们会面。

阿勒颇的一名医生不情愿地承认自己曾治疗过卢卡，但随后命令记者离开，并退还了咨询费。

我们的记者随后在电话簿中预约了另一位医生，这次是在大马士革。 这位医生透露，他曾陪同卢卡的母亲前往俄罗斯就医，但不愿向我们提供更多信息，只是含糊地引导我们前往卢卡女儿之一的药房。

当地人称，自 2024 年 12 月以来，她也没有再出现过。

几个月来，我们在寻找卢卡的过程中一直一片空白。

然后我们取得了第一个突破。

我们再次尝试给书中列出的一位人士打电话，他终于接了电话。

他告诉我们，他曾是卢卡公寓楼的警卫，并最终同意向我们提供他所说的卢卡私人保镖的电话号码——我们称之为马哈茂德。

花了几周时间才获得对马哈茂德的采访。 会议会安排好，但他不会出现，或者他会要求在汽车或公寓等私人空间举行会议，我们的记者认为这样做风险太大。

他们最终在一天晚上午夜之前在一家酒店见面。 马哈茂德肩膀宽阔，体格魁梧，说话前似乎仔细考虑了每一个答案。

他告诉我们，他对卢卡在政权倒台后抛弃他感到愤怒。 马哈茂德告诉我们，随着 2024 年 12 月有消息传出，阿萨德的统治正处于崩溃的边缘，叛军正在向首都挺进，卢卡曾表示他将留下来保卫大马士革。 但马哈茂德说，到第二天凌晨，卢卡就失踪了，并从办公室保险箱中带走了一大笔钱。

马哈茂德拒绝透露卢卡或他家人的任何联系方式，但给了我们卢卡司机的电话号码，他相信当晚司机将这位前间谍头子赶出了首都。

事实证明，这个人更难接近。

当他接电话时，他的声音紧张而不稳定。 他一再坚称自己只是一名司机，对卢卡的活动一无所知。 与我们的多次会面从未保留，最终他不再回复。

我们将注意力转向卢卡可能的逃亡路线，包括邻国黎巴嫩——伊朗支持的真主党在黎巴嫩与阿萨德政权有着密切的联系。

黎巴嫩政府的一位高级消息人士告诉我们，他了解到卢卡在飞往俄罗斯之前持“良好的俄罗斯护照，但名字不同”经过黎巴嫩。

我们设法找到了一名现居黎巴嫩的男子，他的名字列在卢卡的通讯录中，但号码已失效。 由于他与阿萨德政权关系密切，他是叙利亚新政府通缉的众多人之一。

我们无法确认这名男子的身份，他说他有卢卡的电话号码。

我们看到了它，并意识到它有一个俄罗斯国家代码。

俄罗斯是阿萨德政权的主要支持者，阿萨德倒台后几天发表声明，确认他已逃往俄罗斯。 据信他的许多核心圈子都追随了他。

回到卢卡在大马士革的公寓，我们发现了一些线索，表明卢卡与莫斯科也有密切的联系——俄罗斯外国间谍部门颁发的奖项，甚至还有俄罗斯高级官员写给他的新年贺卡。

现在，他的俄罗斯电话号码表明我们终于有证据证明他——正如我们所预测的——在俄罗斯。

我们想验证这个号码确实是卢卡的。

因此，几天后，在我们在场的情况下，该男子同意将他所说的胡萨姆·卢卡 (Hussam Luka) 的人置于免提状态，并根据我们在调查过程中收集到的信息，向他提出一些我们认为只有卢卡才能知道答案的问题。

电话那头的声音听起来有些困惑，但很快又正确地回答了问题。

然而，他拒绝直接与我们交谈。

但我们的联系人后来同意再次给卢卡打电话，并允许我们尝试采访他。

同一声音接听了电话，我们做了自我介绍，解释说我们对有关前政权官员实施的屠杀和酷刑的严重指控有疑问。

“在我现在的处境下，我不能冒任何风险打电话，”卢卡说道，语气很焦虑。

当被问及俄罗斯是否阻止他说话时，卢卡说：“我不能说话。 我无法解释。 你必须明白。”

当被问及是否会在俄罗斯境外与我们见面时，他说：“这很困难。”

然后他就挂了电话。

后来我们获得了第二个号码，我们被告知也是卢卡的——这次是在叙利亚注册的，并链接到他似乎仍在使用的社交媒体和消息应用程序。

经过一天的时间，BBC 在俄罗斯首都莫斯科郊区的两个郊区找到了他。

这些地点似乎与阿萨德流亡俄罗斯时所过的奢华生活方式相去甚远，也与卢卡本人曾经在叙利亚过的生活相去甚远。

我们知道我们无法在俄罗斯亲自接触他，因为阿萨德的追随者在俄罗斯受到国际记者和警察的保护，因此我们决定再次尝试通过电话向他提出指控。

我们拨通了这个号码，接听的声音和以前一样，线路断断续续。

他询问是谁打来的，当被告知是 BBC 时，他立即挂断了电话。

我们通过 WhatsApp 发送消息，要求他对针对他的多项指控做出回应，但他没有回复。

对于那些在叙利亚寻求正义的人来说，确认卢卡在莫斯科是一个艰难的消息。 俄罗斯不太可能从其长期支持的政权中引渡官员。

俄罗斯政府没有回应英国广播公司就卢卡在俄罗斯的存在发表评论的请求，也没有回应是否会考虑引渡请求。

回到霍姆斯，穆罕默德表示，他永远不会放弃卢卡和阿萨德政权其他高级成员有一天会面临正义的希望。

“[我]对所有支持该政权及其安全机构的人感到愤怒...... 他们都反对我们，”他说。

“瓦尔只是一个七岁的孩子...... 他所关心的只是玩耍和享受乐趣。”
